answers.question: How many days of annual leave is a worker entitled to?
answers.answer:
According to the regulations, a worker is entitled to at least thirty days of annual leave for each year of extended service [1]. 

Additionally, the worker is also entitled to two days of annual leave for each month, if their service period is more than six months and less than one year [1]. 

And for part-time workers, the duration of the annual leave is specified in the employment contract, as determined by the Executive Regulation of this Decree by law [1].

answers.question: How long is maternity leave for a female worker?
answers.answer:
The female worker is entitled to maternity leave of sixty days, which includes forty-five days with full pay and fifteen days with half pay [1]. 

The first forty-five days are with full pay, and the following fifteen days are with half pay [1]. 

The female worker may, after using her maternity leave, be absent work without pay for a period not exceeding forty-five consecutive or intermittent days, if such absence is due to an illness suffered by her or her child as a result of pregnancy or childbirth [2]. 

Additionally, if the female worker gives birth after six months or more of pregnancy, she is entitled to an additional thirty days with full pay, and she has the right to extend this leave for an additional thirty days without pay [2].
